messages.content: Write the product page copy for a team chat application, aimed at engineering managers who are choosing between tools. Around 250 words.

# Halyard

You've already got a chat tool. The question is what it takes out of your team's attention budget.

Most chat apps are designed around whoever is typing. Halyard is designed around whoever shows up late — the manager back from two weeks off, the on-call engineer paged at 2am into a channel they have never opened.

**Threads close.** Every thread has a state: open, resolved, handed off. Resolved ones leave your digest. Nobody should have to read 400 messages to learn that Tuesday's deploy got rolled back.

**Search that doesn't stop at chat.** Connect your repos and Halyard indexes PRs, commits, and incident timelines alongside messages. Search `auth timeout` and the argument, the fix, and the postmortem come back in one ranked list.

**Quiet by default.** Notification rules belong to the channel, not to whoever typed @here. Real escalation goes out through PagerDuty or Opsgenie. Chat stops pretending it's a pager.

**The boring questions, answered.** Per-channel retention. SCIM, SAML, audit log export. Data residency in the US, the EU, or your own VPC.

Migration is an afternoon. The importer brings over Slack history, channels, and permissions, and old message permalinks keep resolving, so your runbooks don't quietly rot.

$8 per user per month. Thirty days free, no card. Under ten people on the team? It stays free.

# Halyard

Switching chat tools is a pain. The only reason to do it is that the current one costs your team more attention than it gives back.

Halyard is built for the person who wasn't in the room. Most chat apps optimize for whoever is typing right now. We optimize for the manager returning from PTO to 3,000 unreads, and the on-call engineer paged at 2am into a channel they've never opened.

**Threads have an ending.** Every one is open, resolved, or handed off. Resolved threads drop out of your digest. Learning that Tuesday's deploy got rolled back shouldn't cost you 400 messages.

**Search covers the whole story.** Point Halyard at your repos and it indexes PRs, commits, and incident timelines next to messages. One query for `auth timeout` returns the argument, the fix, and the postmortem, ranked together.

**Quiet is the default.** Channels own their notification rules, not whoever typed @here. Actual escalation routes through PagerDuty or Opsgenie. Your chat app is not your pager.

**Procurement questions, handled.** Retention set per channel. SCIM, SAML, audit log export. Data residency in the US, the EU, or your own VPC.

Moving over takes an afternoon. The importer carries across Slack history, channels, and permissions, and old permalinks keep resolving, so nothing in your runbooks quietly breaks.

$8 per user per month. Thirty days free, no credit card. Teams under ten people stay free.
